learn.title: Passing an array
learn.body: You can give an array to a function. Write the parameter with empty brackets, `int a[]`. The function does not get a copy. It gets the address of the first element, so it works on the caller's real array.

learn.title: The function changes the original
learn.body: `fill` sets every element to 7. After `fill(v, 3, 7)` on `int v[3]`, `main` sees 7 7 7, because no copy was made.

learn.title: Pass the length too
learn.body: An array does not carry its length into a function. The function only knows where it starts. So pass the length as a second argument, as `fill` does with `n`.

learn.title: sizeof inside a function
learn.body: Inside `f`, `a` is just an address, so `sizeof a` is 8 on a 64-bit machine, not 40. The compiler warns about it, which is a useful hint.

learn.title: Promise not to change
learn.body: Write `const int a[]` when a function should only read the array. Then the compiler rejects any attempt to assign to `a[i]` inside it, which protects the caller's data.

learn.title: A reusable sum
learn.body: Write `int sum(const int a[], int n)`.
